Funded by ARPA-E, researchers are developing this technology by testing the concept of directly reducing and alloying concentrated ore to produce steel products. It is estimated that this steelmaking method can reduce energy consumption by at least 50% for producing steel mill products and up to 90% for near-net-shape steel components, which are components manufactured to be as near as possible to the size and shape of the finished product. This process is also conducted at substantially lower temperatures than conventional iron and steel methods, reducing waste heat. To accelerate steel design discovery, Kestrel predicted the structural, magnetic, thermal, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties of new steel products created through melt-less hydrogen-reduction steelmaking.
